how.h2: Three steps, then it runs on its own.

steps.title: Choose your specialties
steps.text: One or several. Physicians, residents, students, dentists, nurses and dietitians each get a feed of their own.

steps.title: Open the feed
steps.text: New review articles every day, ranked for you. Heart the ones you want to keep.

steps.title: Read the paper
steps.text: The original PDF opens inside the app, with highlights and notes, and the article's details one tap away.

product.lead: Short on time and long on standards. Saluxly brings you the paper, not a link farm.

blocks.title: Chosen for you, not for advertisers.
blocks.text: Every paper in your feed is there because of your specialties and what you read, never because someone paid for the spot. No ads, no sponsors, no pharma.
blocks.alt: The feed screen: a list of review articles chosen for the reader's specialties.

blocks.title: The original paper, as the journal published it.
blocks.text: Open-license papers (CC BY and CC0) open inside Saluxly in a native reader. Highlight, take notes and keep them offline. Everything else opens at PubMed Central or the journal’s site, clearly marked.
blocks.alt: The reader screen: the original PDF of a paper with a highlighted passage.

blocks.title: The essentials at a glance. Your AI one tap away.
blocks.text: Aa shows what you need before you open the paper: review type, authors, journal, year, topics and the published abstract. AI sends the PDF to the AI assistant you already use, so you can ask questions or get a summary there. Saluxly itself never sends your reading to an AI.
blocks.alt: The Aa sheet of an article: review type, authors, journal, year, pages, license, topics and the published abstract.

blocks.title: Search that speaks medicine.
blocks.text: Type in English, Spanish or Portuguese, with abbreviations or typos. Saluxly maps your words to medical subject headings and returns the reviews that are about your topic, not the ones that merely mention it.
blocks.alt: The search screen: the query “aspirina preeclampsia prevención” understood as three medical concepts, with the matching reviews.

items.q: Is Saluxly a textbook or a clinical reference?
items.a: No. Saluxly is a reading feed of review articles from the medical literature. It helps you keep up with what is being published in your field; it does not replace a clinical reference, a guideline or your own judgment.

items.q: Where do the articles come from?
items.a: From PubMed, the database of the U.S. National Library of Medicine. Saluxly keeps review articles, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and guidelines from the last five years, published in journals that pass its quality bar.

items.q: Can I read the full paper?
items.a: Yes. Papers with an open license (CC BY or CC0) open inside the app as the original PDF. Other papers open at PubMed Central or on the journal’s website in a browser view, where many are free to read.

items.q: Is it legal to read the PDFs in the app?
items.a: Yes. Saluxly only hosts papers whose license allows it, credits every paper to its authors and journal, and links the rest to their source instead of copying them.

items.q: Which languages does it work in?
items.a: The app runs in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Articles are in English, with titles translated automatically. You can search in any of the three languages.

items.q: Do I need a hospital or university login?
items.a: No. Everything in Saluxly is either openly licensed or free to read at its source. You only need an email address.
iPhone and iPad first, including an iPad layout and a home-screen widget. Android follows, and a web version is planned.

items.q: What do you do with my data?
items.a: Your email signs you in. What you read and save personalizes your feed. Saluxly shows no ads, uses no advertising trackers and does not sell your data. You can delete your account from the app at any time.

final.lead: One email when Saluxly launches on iPhone and iPad. Nothing else.

footer.text: Saluxly is a reading tool for health professionals. It is not a medical device and does not provide medical advice. Article data courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine. Saluxly is not affiliated with or endorsed by the NLM, NIH or HHS.

support.lead: Write to us and a person answers, usually within two business days.

questions.title: Manage or cancel your subscription
questions.text: Subscriptions are billed by Apple. Open Settings on your iPhone, tap your name, then Subscriptions, and choose Saluxly. Cancelling keeps your access until the end of the period you paid for.

questions.title: Restore a purchase on a new device
questions.text: Sign in with the same account, open Profile in the app and tap Restore purchases.

questions.title: An article will not open
questions.text: Papers marked with an outlined page open at PubMed Central or the journal’s website, which can be slow or show its own security check. Try again in a minute, or open the PubMed record from the article details.

questions.title: Change your language, profession or specialties
questions.text: All three live in Profile. Changes apply to your next feed.

support.delete_text: Deleting your account removes your profile, your reading history and your saved articles. Subscriptions are cancelled separately in your App Store settings.
delete_steps: Open Saluxly and go to Profile.
Tap Delete account, at the bottom.
Confirm. Your data is erased within 30 days.
support.delete_mail_after: from the address on your account with the subject “Delete my account”.
